query: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloys are promising bond-coat candidates because of their mechanical properties and elevated-temperature oxidation resistance. Earlier HVAF-M3 work identified 15–45 μm feedstock as optimal for high-quality coatings, but applying the same composition and size range with the HVAF-i7 torch yielded acceptable coating quality yet inadequate thickness. Separate studies of conventional MCrAlY bond coats using the M3 system reported a slight gain in deposition efficiency at higher particle velocity and nozzle-specific best spray distances of 300 and 350 mm. The design target is a sufficiently thick, adherent bond coat that retains coating integrity, minimal as-sprayed oxidation, and durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service, including deposition within internal diameters as small as 120 mm. What single intervention could overcome the thickness limitation? State the hypothesized intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline, define the deposition and service conditions under which it should remain effective, identify supporting evidence from the cited prior studies, and propose a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Increasing the in-flight particle velocity of the FeCoNiCrAl feedstock during HVAF-i7 spraying—by adjusting spray parameters (e.g., optimizing fuel flow and spray distance to around 300–350 mm)—will improve the deposition efficiency and consequently yield a thicker, adherent bond coat with minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
generation.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy feedstock with a particle size of 15–45 μm.
generation.intervention: Adjust HVAF-i7 torch settings to increase the particle velocity (for example, by tuning fuel/oxygen flows and setting the spray distance to 300–350 mm) during deposition.
generation.conditions: Deposition on substrates, including internal diameters as small as 120 mm, under high-temperature thermal-barrier service conditions where oxidation minimization is critical.
generation.structural_mediator: The higher particle velocity increases the kinetic energy of the feedstock particles, which improves their flattening and bonding upon impact with the substrate, leading to enhanced deposit build-up.
generation.mechanism: Enhanced kinetic energy from faster particles results in more effective splat formation and bonding; this increased deposition efficiency overcomes the thickness limitation observed with standard HVAF-i7 parameters, while still maintaining low levels of oxidation.
generation.predicted_outcome: A bond coat with a deposition thickness comparable to that observed using the HVAF-M3 torch, while retaining acceptable oxidation control and adhesion.
generation.baseline: Coatings produced using the HVAF-i7 torch with the standard 15–45 μm feedstock and unoptimized spray parameters, resulting in acceptable quality but inadequate thickness.
generation.boundary: This intervention is expected to be effective when the spray parameters are optimized within the 300–350 mm range and may be limited to systems where particle velocity can be independently increased without adversely affecting other coating properties; applicability outside these specific conditions remains to be verified.
generation.uncertainty: The precise magnitude of the thickness increase and potential impacts on other coating properties (such as oxidation or residual stresses) are uncertain and require experimental validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of FeCoNiCrAl coatings using the HVAF-i7 torch on substrates with internal diameters of 120 mm. Divide the samples into two groups: one using standard HVAF-i7 spray settings (control) and one using optimized settings aimed at increasing particle velocity (targeting spray distances of 300–350 mm). Keep all other parameters (feedstock particle size, substrate preparation, material composition) constant.
measurements: Coating thickness (using cross-sectional microscopy or profilometry)
As-sprayed oxidation level (using X-ray diffraction or oxidation analysis)
In-flight particle velocity (using diagnostic tools such as particle imaging)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coatings produced with the optimized HVAF-i7 parameters do not show a statistically significant increase in thickness relative to the control group—or if the increased particle velocity results in unacceptable adhesion loss or increased oxidation—the hypothesis will be considered falsified.
